title_en: Y2K: The Crisis That Success Erased
title_zh: 千年虫：被成功抹去的危机
english_paragraphs: The Y2K bug, or millennium bug, began as a shortcut. When memory and hardware were costly, programmers stored years as two digits, writing "99" for 1999. That compact code hid an ambiguity: a machine might read "00" as 1900, corrupting calculations of interest, ages, or deadlines.

Governments and firms braced for chaos. In February 1998 President Clinton created a council to coordinate America's effort. Consultants audited legacy systems and patched faulty date logic. In November 1999 the Commerce Department estimated American governments and enterprises would spend about $100bn; projections of the global bill ran to hundreds of billions.

Then midnight struck on 31 December 1999, and little went wrong. Glitches that did crop up were sporadic and mostly minor. Radiation-monitoring equipment faltered at Japan's Shika nuclear plant without any threat to safety, and a Pentagon ground system that processes spy-satellite data failed. In February 2000 a Senate committee concluded that the expenditure had been justified.

Many saw it differently: the threat had been exaggerated, even a hoax. Yet calm prevailed largely because so much had been fixed. This is the preparedness paradox: when precautions work, the danger they ward off never appears, so it looks imaginary. Tedious repairs earned mockery rather than gratitude.

Critics noted that Italy and South Korea spent far less yet fared no worse. The comparison misleads: those low figures often omitted what firms spent, and much of the remedial work replaced obsolete systems overdue for upgrading. Nobody can say which dollars were essential and which excessive. Prevention that works may leave nothing but an invoice, to be weighed against a catastrophe that might have been.
chinese_source_paragraphs: Y2K **漏洞**(bug)，又称**千年**(millennium)虫，起初只是一条**捷径**(shortcut)。当年**内存**(memory)和**硬件**(hardware)都很**昂贵**(costly)，**程序员**(programmers)便把年份存成两位**数字**(digits)，用“99”表示1999年。这种**小而紧凑的**(compact)**代码**(code)暗藏着一种**歧义**(ambiguity)：机器可能把“00”读成1900年，从而**搞错**(corrupting)利息、年龄或**截止日期**(deadlines)的计算。

各国政府和企业都在**严阵以待**(braced for)，**准备迎接**(braced for)一场**混乱**(chaos)。1998年2月，美国**总统**(President)克林顿设立了一个**委员会**(council)来**协调**(coordinate)全美的应对工作。**顾问**(Consultants)们**审查了**(audited)**遗留**(legacy)系统，并**给**(patched)**有缺陷的**(faulty)日期处理逻辑**打上补丁**(patched)。1999年11月，**美国商务部**(Commerce Department)估算，美国各级政府和**企业**(enterprises)将为此花费约1,000亿美元；对**全球**(global)总账单的各种**预测**(projections)则高达数千亿美元。

随后，1999年12月31日的**午夜**(midnight)钟声**敲响**(struck)，几乎没出什么问题。确实**意外出现**(crop up)的**小故障/小毛病**(Glitches)也是**零星的/偶发的**(sporadic)，而且大多**轻微**(minor)。日本志贺核电站的辐射监测设备**出了故障**(faltered)，但并未威胁安全；美国国防部一套处理**间谍**(spy)卫星数据的地面系统也曾失灵。2000年2月，美国参议院的一个委员会**得出结论**(concluded)，认定这笔**开支**(expenditure)是**合理的**(justified)。

许多人却不这么看：在他们眼里，这一威胁被**夸大了**(exaggerated)，甚至是一场**骗局**(hoax)。然而，平静之所以**占据上风**(prevailed)，**很大程度上**(largely)正是因为大量问题早已修好。这就是**防备悖论**(preparedness paradox)：**预防措施**(precautions)一旦奏效，它们所**抵御**(ward off)的危险就永远不会出现，于是看起来像是**虚构的**(imaginary)。那些**枯燥乏味的**(Tedious)修复工作换来的是**嘲笑**(mockery)，而不是**感激**(gratitude)。

批评者指出，意大利和**韩国**(South Korea)花得少得多，结果也**不比别国差**(fared no worse)。但这种**比较**(comparison)**具有误导性**(misleads)：那些低支出数字往往**遗漏了**(omitted)企业自己的花费，而且很大一部分**补救**(remedial)工作替换了**早该**(overdue for)升级的**过时的/淘汰的**(obsolete)系统。谁也说不清哪些钱是**必不可少的**(essential)，哪些是**过度花费的**(excessive)。奏效的**预防**(Prevention)，可能只会留下一张**账单**(invoice)，用来**与**(be weighed against)一场本可能发生的**灾难**(catastrophe)**相权衡**(be weighed against)。

sentences.chinese_source: 这就是**防备悖论**(preparedness paradox)：**预防措施**(precautions)一旦奏效，它们所**抵御**(ward off)的危险就永远不会出现，于是看起来像是**虚构的**(imaginary)。

sentences.english: Tedious repairs earned mockery rather than gratitude.
sentences.chinese_source: 那些**枯燥乏味的**(Tedious)修复工作换来的是**嘲笑**(mockery)，而不是**感激**(gratitude)。

sentences.english: Critics noted that Italy and South Korea spent far less yet fared no worse.
sentences.chinese_source: 批评者指出，意大利和**韩国**(South Korea)花得少得多，结果也**不比别国差**(fared no worse)。

sentences.english: The comparison misleads: those low figures often omitted what firms spent, and much of the remedial work replaced obsolete systems overdue for upgrading.
sentences.chinese_source: 但这种**比较**(comparison)**具有误导性**(misleads)：那些低支出数字往往**遗漏了**(omitted)企业自己的花费，而且很大一部分**补救**(remedial)工作替换了**早该**(overdue for)升级的**过时的/淘汰的**(obsolete)系统。

sentences.english: Nobody can say which dollars were essential and which excessive.
sentences.chinese_source: 谁也说不清哪些钱是**必不可少的**(essential)，哪些是**过度花费的**(excessive)。

sentences.english: Prevention that works may leave nothing but an invoice, to be weighed against a catastrophe that might have been.
sentences.chinese_source: 奏效的**预防**(Prevention)，可能只会留下一张**账单**(invoice)，用来**与**(be weighed against)一场本可能发生的**灾难**(catastrophe)**相权衡**(be weighed against)。

approved_summary: 旧程序为省内存只用两位数字记年，可能将2000年的“00”误读为1900年，算错利息、年龄和期限。
政府与企业排查旧系统、修补日期逻辑；美国1999年预计花约1,000亿美元，全球预测达数千亿美元。
2000年跨年大体平稳，故障零星轻微；美国参议院委员会认定开支合理，却有人把威胁当成骗局。
平稳很大程度上来自预先修复：预防奏效、灾难未现，危险反倒像凭空捏造，这就是“防备悖论”。
意大利、韩国的低支出统计常漏算企业花费，修补也更新了过时系统；究竟哪些钱必要、哪些过量，无法逐笔断定。
